title: Svartsengi uplift passed the level and recharge thresholds of the 2023-2025 Sundhnúkur dike events 5-12 months before October 2026 without a new event; only loads relaxing in 1 year or less agree
abstract: Question: Do the simple uplift and recharge thresholds that timed the ten 2023-2025 Svartsengi dike events (one intrusion, nine Sundhnúkur eruptions) explain why no event followed the July 2025 eruption? Data: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory daily GNSS at SENG (to 17 October 2026), HS02 and NBIO (to 2 May 2026); event dates from the Icelandic Met Office. Method: rolling-origin forecasts that set each rule from earlier cycles only: last pre-event level (R1), level trend (R2), last recharge (R3), recharge trend (R4), and a relaxed-load model in which load decays with time constant tau. Results: By 17 October 2026, SENG was 263 mm above its pre-E9 level, and the recharge since the post-E9 low (436-439 mm) was 39% above the largest earlier recharge (315 mm). No event occurred. At SENG all four threshold rules gave false alarms 159-375 days before the data end; R3, the best rule in cycles E5-E9 (median error 12 days), crossed on 26 February 2026. R1-R3 also failed at HS02 and NBIO. The recharge rate fell at each cycle: the 30-day pre-event rate at SENG went from 8.2 mm/day (E1) to 1.5-2.2 mm/day (E8, E9) and is 0.41-0.46 mm/day now. The open-cycle recharge approaches a limit (475 mm) with a time constant of 201 days, against 112-122 days in E8-E9. The relaxed-load model fitted on E1-E9 does not resolve tau (training error 13.7-15.7 days for tau from 180 days to infinite), but it agrees with no event only for tau of 365 days or less at SENG (270-540 days at the other stations); then the critical SENG rate is 0.7-1.6 mm/day. Limitations: one open cycle; the relaxed-load model was chosen after the outcome was known and failed in rolling tests on E7-E8; in closed cycles the cycle number predicted the needed recharge better than the rate. A nonlinear threshold rise from dike-induced stress changes is not tested.

display.caption: (a) SENG daily vertical position (NGL IGS20, antenna-height corrected) with the ten dike events of 2023-2025 (dotted lines), the level just before each event (triangles), and the open-cycle thresholds from rule R1 (last pre-event level) and R3 (last recharge). Both were crossed months before the data end without a new event. (b) Recharge since each post-event low: closed cycles E1-E9 (blue, dot = event) and the open cycle after E9 (orange) with its exponential fit.

Relaxed-load model fitted on cycles E1-E9: mean absolute onset error against relaxation time tau for three stations. (a) load reset at each event, (b) no reset. Circles: tau values for which the model gives no event in the open cycle to the data end (agrees with observation). Crosses: false alarm. The closed cycles do not resolve tau; the open cycle excludes long tau.

Recharge rates per cycle at SENG, HS02 and NBIO: (a) 40-70 days after the post-event low, (b) last 30 days before each event (open cycle: last 30 days of data). The shaded column is the open cycle after E9.
